stories.title: Anthropic researcher defends AI-assisted Riemann proof, admits rollout missteps
stories.summary: Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge stands by the math in his AI-assisted proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis, but says the 250,000-page claim was a joke and the Lean code is flawed.
stories.more: Alpöge is walking back parts of how he announced the proof, acknowledging he did "stupid things" in the rollout. He clarified that the claim the proof ran to more than 250,000 pages was a joke, not a literal description. He also admitted the published Lean formalization code is, in his words, "full of garbage." Despite the rollout criticism, he maintains that the underlying mathematical result itself still holds.

items.title: Anthropic researcher stands by his AI-assisted Riemann proof but owns up to "stupid things" in the rollout
items.excerpt: Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge is walking back parts of his announcement of an AI-assisted proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis. stories.title: German researchers urge renaming computer science to 'Computer and AI Science'
stories.summary: TU Darmstadt researchers published a position paper calling for computer science to be redefined as 'Computer and AI Science,' citing risks from code generated at runtime.
stories.more: The researchers' central concern is code generated on the fly during runtime, which they argue undermines today's safety and correctness guarantees in software systems. Their position paper frames this as reason enough to redefine the discipline's scope and priorities. The excerpt does not detail specific proposed curriculum or policy changes beyond the renaming call.

stories.title: New paper proposes ViDecide, a decision-centric approach to video diffusion planning
stories.summary: ViDecide reframes video generation as a chain of decisions rather than a fixed-length clip, aiming to fix physical and logical reasoning failures in today's video diffusion models.
stories.more: Current video diffusion models can produce realistic footage but often violate physical and logical constraints during multi-step reasoning and planning tasks, even after reinforcement learning or large-scale training. The paper attributes this to treating a video as a fixed-length clip instead of a chain of decisions. ViDecide instead trains models within a decision-centric framework. The excerpt does not specify benchmark results or release details.

We attribute these failures to the conventional video training paradigm, which treats a solution as a fixed-length clip rather than a chain of decisions. stories.title: SynthDCB benchmark uses world distillation to test AI agents on device control
stories.summary: SynthDCB is a new benchmark for evaluating AI agents on device control, built by distilling device behaviors and environments into reusable components across Home, Car, and Phone domains.
stories.more: The benchmark addresses the challenge of scaling device-control evaluation, which needs both more interactive environments and more tasks for agents to solve. Its 'world distillation' approach converts knowledge of device behaviors, constraints, and environmental effects into modular, executable components. A unified capability representation ties together tool discovery, world execution, and task synthesis. SynthDCB instantiates test environments across Home, Car, and Phone domains. The excerpt does not detail specific benchmark results.

stories.title: Anthropic builds a honeypot to test whether AI agents resist misbehaving
stories.summary: Anthropic created a honeypot-style test to see whether AI agents will go rogue when given the opportunity, and whether they resist the temptation to misbehave.
stories.more: The test is designed around the assumption that AI agents can act against their intended instructions under certain conditions. It evaluates whether agents resist temptation when placed in a scenario built to lure them into misbehavior. Wired's report does not specify which models were tested or what the honeypot scenario involved.

items.title: Anthropic Created a Honeypot to Lure AI Agents Into Misbehaving
items.excerpt: A new test assumes AI agents can go rogue—and asks whether they can resist temptation.

stories.title: Essay argues LLM agents ultimately serve their parent companies, not users
stories.summary: A widely discussed essay argues that LLM-based AI agents are designed to serve the interests of the companies that built them rather than the users deploying them.
stories.more: The piece gained significant traction on Hacker News, with 549 points and 231 comments at time of fetch. The excerpt does not detail the specific examples or arguments the author uses to support the claim, only the essay's core thesis as summarized in its title.

stories.title: Amazon says hackers used AI agents to find and exploit a 0-day with little help
stories.summary: Amazon reported that attackers used AI agents, built on the Cairn AI framework, to discover and exploit a zero-day vulnerability with minimal human guidance.
stories.more: The incident highlights how the same agentic AI frameworks used by defenders, such as Cairn AI, can also be weaponized by attackers for vulnerability discovery and exploitation. Ars Technica reports the AI agents required little human input to find and exploit the flaw. The excerpt does not name the affected system or disclose further technical details.

items.title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
items.excerpt: The Cairn AI framework is proving to be a boon for defenders and attackers.

stories.title: Amazon acquires Decart for $7.5B to narrow AI chip efficiency gap with Nvidia
stories.summary: Amazon bought AI startup Decart in a reported $7.5 billion deal aimed at using software to make its Trainium chips more efficient against Nvidia's hardware.
stories.more: The acquisition reflects Amazon's strategy of pairing software improvements with its custom Trainium chips rather than competing on raw hardware alone. TechCrunch frames the deal, reportedly worth $7.5 billion, as part of a broader effort to close the efficiency gap with Nvidia in the AI chip race. The excerpt does not detail what specific technology Decart contributes or the acquisition's timeline.

items.excerpt: Amazon’s decision to acquire Decart for a reported $7.5 billion is part of its efforts to improve the efficiency of its Trainium chips.

Trump and Vance are named as having applied pressure on the board. The excerpt does not detail why Huang was originally removed or the timeline of the reinstatement.

stories.title: Pinterest adds parental controls to limit AI-generated content shown to teens
stories.summary: Pinterest is rolling out a feature letting parents restrict how much AI-generated content their teenage children see, addressing AI content in feeds rather than chatbot access.
stories.more: The move contrasts with other social platforms, which have mostly focused on restricting teens' access to AI chatbots rather than the AI-generated content filling their feeds. The excerpt does not specify how the limit is implemented or when it rolls out broadly.

stories.title: Insiders say OpenAI and Anthropic's unreleased models have outgrown safety measures
stories.summary: An Axios report cites dozens of OpenAI and Anthropic employees who believe their companies' unreleased frontier models can no longer be safely controlled, with internal debate over halting releases.
stories.more: The report says staff at both companies are increasingly worried that frontier models in development have exceeded what current safety measures can handle. Internally, employees are debating whether to pause releases or stop training further models altogether. The Decoder notes that trust in leadership is eroding among employees at both companies. The excerpt does not specify which particular models or safety measures are referenced.

stories.title: Crusoe investor bets on solar and batteries to power future AI data centers
stories.summary: An investor in cloud provider Crusoe argues that solar power and battery storage are the practical choice for the tens of gigawatts future AI data centers will need.
stories.more: The investor's thesis centers on next-generation data centers needing tens of gigawatts of power annually, a scale that strains conventional grid and generation options. Solar paired with battery storage is framed as a faster-to-deploy alternative to the gas turbines and nuclear projects other data center operators are pursuing. TechCrunch's report does not name the investor or specify dollar amounts involved.

items.title: Why a Crusoe investor is betting on solar and batteries to power future AI data centers
items.excerpt: Next-generation data centers will need tens of gigawatts of power every year. One of Crusoe's investors thinks solar and energy storage are the obvious choice.

stories.title: Report: agentic AI is driving a surge in enterprise network traffic and strain
stories.summary: AI deployment, and now agentic AI specifically, is becoming the biggest driver of enterprise network demand, with AI agent tasks generating an estimated 450% more traffic than the same tasks done by humans.
stories.more: The report notes that enterprise networks are under severe strain as companies rush to deploy AI, with agentic AI adding further load on top of existing demand. It cites an estimate that tasks performed by AI agents generate about 450% more network traffic than equivalent tasks done by human workers. The excerpt does not specify which companies or network vendors are involved, or what modernization steps are recommended.

stories.more: The video, with nearly 6 million views, shows an AI-generated Huang dancing in a club before a depiction of Alice Huang - described as a Chinese technology executive and suspected spy - appears beside him. The Verge frames the clip as part of a broader trend of AI deepfakes spreading as viral entertainment content. The excerpt does not specify who created the deepfake or whether Huang has responded.
